newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says Turkey releases tourist couple.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says Turkey releases tourist couple.

text.p: A Polish-American man and a Polish woman abducted by Kurds in Turkey, then arrested by Turkish authorities after their release, are now free, the State Department said on Thursday.

Christopher Mrozowski and his Polish fiancee, identified in Polish news reports as Magdalena Glowacka, were seized from a bus in eastern Turkey on Sept. 24 by Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) guerrillas.

Released three days later, they were arrested by Turkish authorities on charges of assisting a terrorist organisation. The Turkish government has been fighting a bloody decade-long war against the separatist PKK.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said the two were released on Wednesday from a prison in the town of Batman. They were given back their passports and U.S. and Polish officials escorted them to an airport, he said.
"We understand that the case against them has not been closed, but they will not be required to return to Turkey for legal proceedings," Burns added.
Mrozowski has been identified in U.S. media reports as a former University of Maryland instructor whose mother lives in Bethesda, Maryland. He holds dual Polish and U.S. citizenship.
There was no word on the fate of an Iranian man who was reported to be with Mrozowski and Glowacka.
